GlossaryPage_def_1: A system that sets the minimum wage level for workers by law and compels employers to pay at least this amount, with the state intervening in the wage-setting process between labor and management.
GlossaryPage_ex_1: As of 2026, the legal minimum hourly wage applies to all workplaces; violations can lead to up to 3 years in prison or fines of up to 20 million KRW.
GlossaryPage_def_2: The most basic contract wage excluding additional allowances, based on job performance ability, skills, responsibilities, age, or years of service.
GlossaryPage_ex_2: The fixed monthly amount specified in the employment contract, serving as the base rate for calculating bonuses and overtime/night/holiday allowances.
GlossaryPage_def_3: The hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or piece-rate amount promised to be paid to a worker regularly, uniformly, and fixedly for prescribed or total labor.
GlossaryPage_ex_3: Used as the basis for calculating overtime, night work, holiday work, annual paid leave, and layoff notice allowances.
GlossaryPage_def_4: A payment method where the wage is fixed as a set amount every month, regardless of the number of days in the month (28-31) or the number of holidays.
GlossaryPage_ex_4: Applicable to general office workers or fixed-schedule employees; the full base salary is paid as long as there are no absences.
GlossaryPage_def_5: A payment method calculating wages based on the hourly rate for actual hours worked. Wages are proportional to hours worked.
GlossaryPage_ex_5: Mainly used for part-time jobs or shift-work manufacturing positions, calculated as [Actual Hours Worked × Hourly Rate].
GlossaryPage_def_6: A method where the wage is set and paid on a daily basis, compensating for the labor provided during that specific day.
GlossaryPage_ex_6: Applied to construction site workers, daily laborers, or short-term contractors; often settled immediately after the day's work.
GlossaryPage_def_7: A method where wages are calculated and paid weekly based on the previous week's performance and the agreed-upon weekly wage rate.
GlossaryPage_ex_7: Commonly used in certain short-term project sites, by freelancers, or in North American overseas workplaces.
GlossaryPage_def_8: A wage system paid regularly and fixedly every month, regardless of personal sales performance, company results, or fluctuations in total monthly hours.
GlossaryPage_ex_8: Includes base salary and regular, fixed monthly meal allowances or vehicle maintenance allowances paid without conditions.
GlossaryPage_def_9: Wage items that fluctuate monthly based on a worker's performance, output, work record, or the amount of overtime/extra work done that month.
GlossaryPage_ex_9: Includes personal incentives, sales commissions, overtime pay, night work allowance, and company performance bonuses.
GlossaryPage_def_10: The total sum of salary and allowances paid regularly and fixedly every month, used as a reference for determining tax-exempt income under tax law.
GlossaryPage_ex_10: The amount derived by adding the base salary and fixed allowances (position allowance, technical allowance, etc.) and excluding irregular items like overtime pay.
GlossaryPage_def_11: The total taxable amount before deductions, derived by subtracting tax-exempt income (like meal allowances) from the total wage received from the employer.
GlossaryPage_ex_11: The standard amount for year-end tax settlement or income tax calculation, similar to the pre-tax annual salary concept.
GlossaryPage_def_12: The final amount the worker receives directly into their bank account after all taxes (income tax, local income tax) and social insurance (national pension, health, employment insurance) are deducted.
GlossaryPage_ex_12: The result of [Total Payment - Total Deductions] on the pay stub; the net monthly salary available for spending or savings.
GlossaryPage_def_13: The total contract payment amount before legal deductions such as income tax, resident tax, and social insurance premiums are collected.
GlossaryPage_ex_13: The sum of base salary plus all allowances like overtime and meal expenses; usually the standard wage written in an employment contract.
GlossaryPage_def_14: The amount remaining after withholding taxes and social insurance premiums are subtracted from pre-tax salary; synonymous with net salary.
GlossaryPage_ex_14: Even if the contract is for a pre-tax salary of 3 million KRW, if 300,000 KRW is deducted for taxes and insurance, the net salary is 2.7 million KRW.
GlossaryPage_def_15: All money or goods paid by an employer to a worker in exchange for labor, regardless of what it is named (Labor Standards Act, Article 2).
GlossaryPage_ex_15: Regardless of whether it is called an allowance or a bonus, if it is paid by an employer to a worker in a subordinate relationship for labor, it is recognized as wages.
GlossaryPage_def_16: A general term for all remuneration systems received regularly (usually on a specific day of the month) from a company or employer in exchange for work.
GlossaryPage_ex_16: Processed via bulk bank transfer to the worker's salary account on the 25th of every month, as specified in the company's employment rules.
GlossaryPage_def_17: A taxable income concept used under social insurance laws (employment/health insurance) to calculate insurance premiums from wages received for labor.
GlossaryPage_ex_17: The Health Insurance Corporation calculates the average monthly remuneration by excluding tax-exempt income and applying it to insurance premiums.
GlossaryPage_def_18: The total sum of all wage items, such as base salary, allowances, and bonuses, paid to a worker over a specific period.
GlossaryPage_ex_18: The total wage amount over three months, which serves as the basis for calculating average wages.
GlossaryPage_def_19: Individual or combined amounts of all allowances and salary items provided by an employer to a worker in exchange for labor and benefits.
GlossaryPage_ex_19: Usually located on the left column of the pay stub, representing the total amount the employer promised to pay, including base salary, meal allowance, etc.
GlossaryPage_def_20: The amount an employer deducts from a monthly salary in advance for legal deductions like income tax and social insurance premiums, as per the Labor Standards Act.
GlossaryPage_ex_20: Included in the deduction details on the right side of the pay stub, such as National Pension, Health Insurance, Employment Insurance, and Income Tax.
GlossaryPage_def_21: An additional premium paid for work exceeding statutory working hours (8 hours/day, 40 hours/week) or hours agreed upon by both parties.
GlossaryPage_ex_21: In workplaces with 5+ employees, overtime pay must be 150% (50% surcharge on top of the hourly wage) for extra hours worked.
GlossaryPage_def_22: An additional allowance paid for labor provided between 10 PM and 6 AM, which is designated as night work hours under the Labor Standards Act.
GlossaryPage_ex_22: If a night shift worker works during these hours, they receive an additional 50% surcharge on their hourly wage by law.
GlossaryPage_def_23: An additional wage paid to workers for working on statutory paid holidays (weekly holidays, Labor Day, public holidays, etc.) or agreed-upon holidays.
GlossaryPage_ex_23: In workplaces with 5+ employees, working up to 8 hours on a holiday incurs a 50% surcharge; exceeding 8 hours incurs a 100% surcharge.
GlossaryPage_def_24: An allowance for one or more paid holidays given to workers who have worked 15+ hours per week and have perfect attendance for the agreed-upon workdays.
GlossaryPage_ex_24: If you attend work perfectly for 5 days a week, you receive one day's worth of wages (8 hours) included in your salary, even without working on Sunday.
GlossaryPage_def_25: An allowance that monetarily compensates for annual paid leave days that were not used and have expired after one year under the Labor Standards Act.
GlossaryPage_ex_25: If 5 days of annual leave remain at the end of the year or upon retirement, they are settled as [5 days × 1 day's standard wage] and added to the salary.
GlossaryPage_def_26: An allowance paid separately from the base salary, considering the nature, difficulty, responsibility, or uniqueness of a specific job performed.
GlossaryPage_ex_26: A monthly job allowance of 100,000 KRW is paid to main-line workers responsible for precision inspection or handling special chemical substances.
GlossaryPage_def_27: An allowance for contributors in managerial roles within the corporate hierarchy, such as team leaders, group leaders, or foremen, who hold specific responsibilities.
GlossaryPage_ex_27: Production foremen who manage foreign staff and give work orders receive an additional allowance for their management role.
GlossaryPage_def_28: An allowance paid to workers who hold nationally certified technical qualifications or professional licenses essential or useful for their job duties.
GlossaryPage_ex_28: Paid to a technician who has submitted an electrician certification and been appointed as a fire safety manager for factory facility management.
GlossaryPage_def_29: An incentive allowance for engineers or technical workers with specific technical know-how, high proficiency, or specialized process operation capabilities.
GlossaryPage_ex_29: Technical allowances are granted based on company standards to highly skilled foreign workers capable of special precision welding or CNC lathe programming.
GlossaryPage_def_30: An amount paid to compensate for risk-taking when the workplace or environment involves high possibilities of disasters, such as physical danger, high heat, or toxic gas exposure.
GlossaryPage_ex_30: Allowances are added when participating in high-risk industrial processes, such as work near high-voltage lines or installing high-rise external scaffolding.
GlossaryPage_def_31: A welfare benefit provided as a fixed amount or reimbursement to cover fuel costs, tolls, or public transportation for a worker's daily commute.
GlossaryPage_ex_31: Regular support of 150,000 KRW for long-distance commuters or non-carpoolers included in salary items.
GlossaryPage_def_32: An amount provided to cover meal costs during working hours, a representative tax-exempt allowance excluded from taxation up to 200,000 KRW per month.
GlossaryPage_ex_32: Separating 200,000 KRW as a meal allowance in salary items creates tax-saving effects by reducing the total subject to income tax and social insurance.
GlossaryPage_def_33: An incentive allowance paid proportionally to the number of years of service to encourage long-term commitment and loyalty.
GlossaryPage_ex_33: A welfare salary item that accumulates 20,000 KRW every year or increases regularly upon reaching the 3rd or 5th year.
GlossaryPage_def_34: An allowance paid based on the number of family members (spouse, children, parents) according to company regulations, to support living expenses.
GlossaryPage_ex_34: Paid monthly after confirming the resident registration, such as 30,000 KRW for a spouse and 20,000 KRW per child.
GlossaryPage_def_35: Bonus-like money paid additionally at specific times (holidays, year-end, etc.) or according to company rules, besides regular base salary and allowances.
GlossaryPage_ex_35: If the employment rules specify [400% annual bonus split payment], bonuses are settled regularly during Seollal, Chuseok, and summer vacations.
GlossaryPage_def_36: Incentive money distributed differently based on the achievement rate of annual profit goals, department evaluation results, or individual productivity scores.
GlossaryPage_ex_36: Case where 200% of the base salary is paid to all employees as a performance bonus following a Profit Sharing (PS) plan after exceeding the production target by 120%.
GlossaryPage_def_37: A general term for all supplementary wage items added to the base salary to cover job uniqueness, special working conditions, or welfare benefits.
GlossaryPage_ex_37: Includes vehicle maintenance, hygiene allowances, overtime pay, etc., listed below the base salary line in the pay stub payment items.
GlossaryPage_def_38: An allowance that must be paid by adding a legal surcharge on top of normal labor compensation when performing work outside of standards (overtime, night, holiday).
GlossaryPage_ex_38: In 5+ employee firms, 1 hour of overtime must be settled at 1.5 times the normal wage by adding a 50% surcharge.
GlossaryPage_def_39: Fixed allowances that are paid 100% unconditionally every month regardless of actual attendance or monthly production performance.
GlossaryPage_ex_39: Position allowances or qualification appointment allowances, which are paid as a fixed 100,000 KRW according to contract conditions regardless of whether you worked 15 or 20 days.
GlossaryPage_def_40: Non-fixed allowances where the requested and paid amount varies frequently based on monthly overtime hours, daily attendance, or sales commissions.
GlossaryPage_ex_40: Representative non-fixed allowances include overtime/night work allowances that change every month based on actual hours worked.
GlossaryPage_def_41: Working hours promised by both parties in an employment contract (e.g., 'Let's work this many hours a day') within the legal standard working hours.
GlossaryPage_ex_41: If the contract says [Working hours: 09:00~18:00, including 1 hour break], the daily prescribed working hours are 8 hours excluding lunch.
GlossaryPage_def_42: The maximum working hours enforced by national law under Article 50 of the Labor Standards Act; generally cannot exceed 40 hours/week or 8 hours/day.
GlossaryPage_ex_42: Even if the employer sets 10 hours in the contract, the 2 hours exceeding the 8-hour legal limit must be paid as overtime.
GlossaryPage_def_43: The act of providing labor beyond the prescribed hours promised in the contract. For full-time 5-day workers, any hours over 40 per week apply.
GlossaryPage_ex_43: Working until 8 PM after 6 PM to meet factory output targets, while providing labor to check the operating line for 2 extra hours.
GlossaryPage_def_44: Labor provided between 10 PM (22:00) and 6 AM (06:00), which is designated as a time of increased physical fatigue under the Labor Standards Act.
GlossaryPage_ex_44: A night shift worker performing part assembly at 2 AM is engaged in legal night work.
GlossaryPage_def_45: Work performed on holidays (weekly holidays, public holidays, etc.) or designated days off, when work duties are originally exempted.
GlossaryPage_ex_45: Working from 9 AM to 6 PM on Sunday due to a delay in finishing a production process on Saturday, even though Sunday is a designated paid holiday.
GlossaryPage_def_46: A method of rotating working hours in cycles, dividing workers into 2+ groups to allow 24-hour operation or extended production hours.
GlossaryPage_ex_46: A 2-group 2-shift system where Group A works day shifts (08:00~20:00) this week, Group B works night shifts (20:00~08:00), and they swap the following week.
GlossaryPage_def_47: A flexible working system where hours are increased in some weeks and decreased in others to balance out.
GlossaryPage_ex_47: Used when temporarily extending working hours during peak seasons when work is concentrated.
GlossaryPage_def_48: A system where workers decide their own daily arrival/departure times within a 1-month settlement period, averaging 40 hours/week.
GlossaryPage_ex_48: An autonomous working system where if you satisfy the core time (11:00~15:00), you can work 4 hours on Monday and make up for it by working 12 hours on Thursday.
GlossaryPage_def_49: A system that maintains a standard 5-day, 8-hour work schedule but shifts arrival/departure times by group to accommodate individual convenience or congestion.
GlossaryPage_ex_49: Group 1 works 08:00~17:00, Group 2 works 10:00~19:00 to separate on-site operations.
GlossaryPage_def_50: Legally guaranteed time during working hours for freedom from employer supervision, used for breaks or meals, excluded from wage calculation time.
GlossaryPage_ex_50: Since 30-60 minutes of break time must be given after 4-8 hours of work under the Labor Standards Act, most factories designate 12:00~13:00 as lunch/break time.
GlossaryPage_def_51: Time when a worker waits for the next work order under employer supervision, even without providing actual labor. Included in working time, not break time.
GlossaryPage_ex_51: The 1 hour that staff waited at the site because raw materials didn't arrive on time before work started must be paid as working time.
GlossaryPage_def_52: Time purely dedicated to actual labor, such as operating machines, processing materials, or packaging products at a production site.
GlossaryPage_ex_52: Pure production run time recorded in the ERP system after the worker logs in and starts the line.
GlossaryPage_def_53: Total time providing labor under employer supervision, including preparation and waiting time, not just active machine operating time.
GlossaryPage_ex_53: Total contract time, excluding the 1-hour lunch break, from morning roll call to cleaning time, which is the basis for salary calculation.
GlossaryPage_def_54: All working forms performed exceeding the statutory prescribed working hours specified in employment rules or contracts, covering overtime, night, and holiday work.
GlossaryPage_ex_54: Total cumulative time worked after completing the 40-hour base workweek, including Saturday special work or working late on weekdays.
GlossaryPage_def_55: A term for overtime work done after regular hours to process remaining inventory or meet additional production needs.
GlossaryPage_ex_55: Working an extra 2 hours until 8 PM after regular 6 PM departure to meet container shipment volume.
GlossaryPage_def_56: Abbreviation for 'Special Work', an overtime holiday work form involving reporting to work on weekends (Sat/Sun) or holidays designated by the company/law.
GlossaryPage_ex_56: Working a special shift from 9 AM to 6 PM this Sunday due to the factory operation schedule.
GlossaryPage_def_57: Arriving and checking in/recording at the workplace later than the prescribed start time designated in the contract.
GlossaryPage_ex_57: Required to be at the site by 9 AM, but checked in at 9:15 AM after missing the commute bus.
GlossaryPage_def_58: Leaving the workplace before the prescribed end time with prior approval from a manager due to personal or health reasons.
GlossaryPage_ex_58: Leaving for the hospital at 3 PM after reporting a sudden fever, despite a 6 PM end time.
GlossaryPage_def_59: State of not reporting to work or providing labor on a day with a work obligation (prescribed workday). Classified as approved absence or unauthorized absence.
GlossaryPage_ex_59: Taking a day off after submitting a leave/absence request due to personal reasons or moving.
GlossaryPage_def_60: Comprehensive records of faithfulness and status regarding attendance, departure, tardiness, leaving early, and absence.
GlossaryPage_ex_60: HR manager downloads monthly tardiness/absence data of foreign workers from the attendance management system before payroll calculation.
GlossaryPage_def_61: Manual ledger or digital management software used to daily record/prove attendance and departure times.
GlossaryPage_ex_61: Forms using time card machines at the site office entrance or smartphone GPS apps for attendance stamps.
GlossaryPage_def_62: A statutory paid holiday that must be granted at least once a week to those who have perfect attendance for the prescribed workdays of that week.
GlossaryPage_ex_62: If you attended work perfectly from Monday to Friday, Sunday becomes a paid weekly holiday where you receive one day's basic salary even without working.
GlossaryPage_def_63: Statutory or company-agreed holiday where labor duty is exempted, but 100% of the standard wage is paid without deduction.
GlossaryPage_ex_63: May 1st (Labor Day) is a mandatory paid holiday; reducing salary even if the factory shuts down constitutes wage arrears.
GlossaryPage_def_64: A day designated as a non-work day, but unlike paid holidays, a daily wage or salary preservation is not granted.
GlossaryPage_ex_64: In a 5-day workweek company, if Saturday is designated as an unpaid day off, it is a day off, but no separate daily wage is paid.
GlossaryPage_def_65: National 'red days' designated by government regulations, now mandatory as paid holidays even for private businesses with 5+ employees.
GlossaryPage_ex_65: Chuseok, Seollal holidays, March 1st (Independence Movement Day), Liberation Day, etc., marked in red on the calendar.
GlossaryPage_def_66: 15+ days of paid leave granted legally for perfect attendance (80%+) for one year, allowing workers to rest without loss of pay at their desired time.
GlossaryPage_ex_66: Received 15 days of annual leave this year for perfect attendance last year, used 5 consecutive days during summer vacation to visit hometown.
GlossaryPage_def_67: Leave requested and granted with a doctor's note when normal attendance is impossible due to non-work-related illnesses, injuries, or accidents.
GlossaryPage_ex_67: Treatment during a 2-week approved sick leave after submitting an orthopedic diagnosis for a leg fracture sustained during weekend activities.
GlossaryPage_def_68: Leave guaranteed according to company rules for happy or sad family events (marriage, birth, parent's death, etc.).
GlossaryPage_ex_68: 3 to 5 days of paid consolation leave granted when a foreign worker's parent passes away.
GlossaryPage_def_69: Special leave granted at management's discretion or labor-management agreement for company founding anniversaries, awards, or special circumstances.
GlossaryPage_ex_69: Granted 1 day of special reward leave for selection as a superior production contribution team, allowing a Friday off without using annual leave.
GlossaryPage_def_70: Administrative state where the employment relationship is maintained, but work duty is justifiably exempted or stopped for a period.
GlossaryPage_ex_70: Contract maintaining employment status after 3 months of leave approved by the company for long-term treatment or resolving personal issues back home.
GlossaryPage_def_71: A long-term legal leave system for male/female workers to raise children aged 8 or under (or 2nd grade or under in elementary).
GlossaryPage_ex_71: Applying to the Ministry of Employment and Labor to take up to 1 year of leave to raise children, receiving childcare leave benefits from employment insurance.
GlossaryPage_def_72: An illegal attendance act of unilaterally not reporting to work without any prior contact or justification to the company/manager.
GlossaryPage_ex_72: Sustained unauthorized absence for 3+ consecutive days without contact can become grounds for disciplinary dismissal under internal rules.
GlossaryPage_def_73: A linked leave system where one day off is designated on a normal working day in exchange for working on a designated holiday.
GlossaryPage_ex_73: Designated Wednesday as a substitute holiday for working last Sunday due to a factory line inspection.
GlossaryPage_def_74: System under Article 57 of the Labor Standards Act, granting leave (at a 1.5x rate) instead of paying overtime/night/holiday wages in money.
GlossaryPage_ex_74: Instead of paying 1.5x cash for 8 hours of overtime, it is accumulated as 1.5 days of paid leave.
GlossaryPage_def_75: A form for requesting leave (type, desired date, reason, emergency contact) and obtaining approval from a superior.
GlossaryPage_ex_75: Submitted leave application listing annual leave plans for a hometown visit, receiving final approval from the on-site supervisor.
GlossaryPage_def_76: A legal provision for exchanging a statutory holiday with a normal working day by mutual agreement at least 24 hours in advance.
GlossaryPage_ex_76: Agreement reached with worker representatives to work normally this Sunday (holiday) and designate next Monday as a paid holiday instead.
GlossaryPage_def_77: Legal contract document stating that a worker provides labor and the company pays wages; must specify wages, hours, holidays, and annual leave in writing.
GlossaryPage_ex_77: On the first day of work, signed 2 copies of the employment contract (stating hourly wage/hours) with HR and kept one.
GlossaryPage_def_78: Standard form distributed by the Ministry of Employment and Labor, mandatory for Employment Permit System (E-9) foreign workers to prevent violations.
GlossaryPage_ex_78: Non-professional employment workers entering through the EPS system sign the standard contract electronically with the Korean employer in their home country.
GlossaryPage_def_79: Essential standards of labor conditions decided upon signing: wage amount/payment method, prescribed hours, holidays, leave, work location, and duties.
GlossaryPage_ex_79: Core conditions in the contract: 10,000 KRW/hour, 5-day workweek, dormitory provision, etc., as specified in the recruitment announcement.
GlossaryPage_def_80: HR action of finalizing employment after processes such as recruitment, interviews, and evaluation to secure necessary personnel.
GlossaryPage_ex_80: Announced recruitment for 5 new foreign workers to secure production line operators for the second-half factory expansion.
GlossaryPage_def_81: The act of a successfully recruited worker reporting for duty, initiating the employment contract's validity, and starting their first day.
GlossaryPage_ex_81: New members who passed all reviews report for duty at 8 AM next Monday for orientation.
GlossaryPage_def_82: Initial educational/probationary period set to improve or observe a worker's proficiency, job performance, and adaptability after employment.
GlossaryPage_ex_82: For contracts of 1+ year, a 3-month probation period is allowed, during which paying 90% of the minimum wage is permitted.
GlossaryPage_def_83: A preliminary observation period to test a worker's qualifications, personality, and site suitability before finalizing the main contract.
GlossaryPage_ex_83: If clear disqualifications like unauthorized absence or failure to adapt are found during the 2-month trial period, the main contract can be rightfully refused.
GlossaryPage_def_84: The total legally binding employment period from the start date to the automatic expiration date.
GlossaryPage_ex_84: Signed contract specifying exactly 1 year: [June 1, 2026 to May 31, 2027].
GlossaryPage_def_85: Act of extending the contract period by mutual agreement upon the expiration of the existing contract to continue the employment relationship.
GlossaryPage_ex_85: Held a consultation with a high-performing non-regular worker whose contract ends this month, then drafted contract renewal documents.
GlossaryPage_def_86: Contract form maintaining the same core conditions as the existing contract but extending the expiration date to secure an additional period.
GlossaryPage_ex_86: Received additional signatures on an extension contract adding 3 months to the expiration date (from June to September) for contract workers due to volume increase.
GlossaryPage_def_87: Contract re-signed during the existing period or at renewal by changing core conditions like hourly wage, location, or job description.
GlossaryPage_ex_87: Issued new salary change contract for next year, reflecting the minimum wage increase and promotion to group leader.
GlossaryPage_def_88: Specific type of labor and scope of duties a worker must perform upon joining, a mandatory legal item in the contract.
GlossaryPage_ex_88: Specified 'Injection molding machine operation and plastic part quality visual inspection' in the duty description column.
GlossaryPage_def_89: A concept more detailed than duties, referring to individual task details on a daily work instruction sheet.
GlossaryPage_ex_89: Detailed duties for warehouse staff: hoist crane operation, inputting incoming/outgoing goods, and monthly inventory surveys.
GlossaryPage_def_90: The specific geographical location or business site address where a worker must report and perform work.
GlossaryPage_ex_90: Specified working location as [PayLens Factory 2, Production Bldg A, Munsan-eup, Paju-si, Gyeonggi-do] in the contract.
GlossaryPage_def_91: Measure to change a worker's duties or shift based on management needs,공정 restructuring, or the worker's consent.
GlossaryPage_ex_91: Issued reassignment order for 2 skilled foreign workers to the press process line due to excess assembly line personnel.
GlossaryPage_def_92: Employment form where the employment relationship is with a dispatch agency, but labor is directed/supervised by the client company (original contractor).
GlossaryPage_ex_92: Received 3 dispatched workers from an agency for 3 months to support on-site loading volume, directing them in the warehouse.
GlossaryPage_def_93: HR measure of changing a worker's long-term location within the same corporation (e.g., HQ to branch, Factory 1 to Factory 2).
GlossaryPage_ex_93: Transferred a veteran management engineer from the HQ factory to the Sejong branch for the stable setup of the new Chungcheong-do factory.
GlossaryPage_def_94: HR disciplinary action or management policy of unilaterally terminating the employment relationship permanently.
GlossaryPage_ex_94: Unilateral dismissal without just cause is illegal; 5+ employee firms must notify 30 days prior or provide written notice.
GlossaryPage_def_95: Method where the company recommends resignation due to management difficulties/disqualification, and the worker agrees, ending the contract by mutual consent.
GlossaryPage_ex_95: Company suggested resignation due to line reduction, and since the worker agreed to the severance package, it qualifies for unemployment benefits.
GlossaryPage_def_96: Purely voluntary act of the worker submitting a resignation letter due to personal reasons (job change, study, health, return home) without pressure.
GlossaryPage_ex_96: Submitted resignation with handover documents one month in advance due to personal reasons and an confirmed offer from another company.
GlossaryPage_def_97: Visa type/grade under immigration law determining the foreign worker's allowed scope of employment activities in Korea.
GlossaryPage_ex_97: Factory workers under the employment permit system receive Non-Professional Employment (E-9), while student visas (D-2) cannot work full-time without permission.
GlossaryPage_def_98: Legal expiration date of the stay period permitted by the Immigration Office chief for a foreigner to stay in Korea.
GlossaryPage_ex_98: Expiration date on the back of the Foreign Registration Card is Dec 31, 2026; must apply for extension before this date to avoid fines.
GlossaryPage_def_99: Judicial administrative act approved by the Minister of Justice, allowing a foreigner to normally perform activities (employment, training) consistent with their entry purpose.
GlossaryPage_ex_99: Obtained final stay permission stamp/electronic record for extended employment activities after thorough immigration office review.
GlossaryPage_def_100: General term under immigration law for all profitable economic activities where a foreigner enters a contract with a Korean entity and receives wages.
GlossaryPage_ex_100: E-9 holders are prohibited from taking side jobs in restaurants or delivery, which violates immigration law.
GlossaryPage_def_101: Short-term employment status (visa) for foreign workers entering via EPS, limited to site-based work in manufacturing, construction, agriculture, etc.
GlossaryPage_ex_101: E-9 workers cannot change workplaces at will; they must go through legal procedures and receive Employment Center approval to transfer.
GlossaryPage_def_102: National system for managing the legal employment of foreign workers by SMEs that cannot find domestic personnel, permitted by the government (MOEL).
GlossaryPage_ex_102: According to EPS purpose, employers must fulfill the domestic hiring effort duty for 7-14 days before applying for foreign personnel.
GlossaryPage_def_103: Administrative permit certificate issued by the Employment Center stating an employer is permitted to legally hire a foreign worker.
GlossaryPage_ex_103: Must obtain an Employment Permit Certificate to move to the stage of signing the standard labor contract with the foreign worker.
GlossaryPage_def_104: Administrative procedure of reporting to the MOEL and Immigration Office regarding employment changes when a foreign worker joins, changes status, etc.
GlossaryPage_ex_104: Must complete employment/change reports within 15 days of the occurrence to avoid administrative fines.
GlossaryPage_def_105: Illegal act of hiring foreigners without work visas or deploying personnel without formal government permits.
GlossaryPage_ex_105: Deploying tourists (B-1, B-2) or students (D-2) to the factory line without prior employment activity permission is subject to punishment for illegal hiring.
GlossaryPage_def_106: State of a foreigner staying in Korea without permission after their visa expiration, violating immigration law.
GlossaryPage_ex_106: Staying in a factory zone without visa extension permission leads to forced deportation and entry restriction.
GlossaryPage_def_107: Procedure where, under immigration or EPS law, prior documents must be submitted and approval obtained before certain acts (status change, adding workplace).
GlossaryPage_ex_107: In principle, prior permission must be obtained before beginning changed activities when converting to a different visa.
GlossaryPage_def_108: Administrative application to extend the stay validity deadline to continue residing in Korea for the same purpose after the visa expires.
GlossaryPage_ex_108: Can apply for stay extension review via the immigration portal 4 months before visa expiration following contract renewal.
GlossaryPage_def_109: Immigration procedure of canceling the current status (visa) and converting to a different type to change the scope of activities.
GlossaryPage_ex_109: Case where an E-9 worker applies for status change to Skilled Worker (E-7-4) for long-term employment based on performance and proficiency.
GlossaryPage_def_110: Term for acts of crossing borders (entry/exit) and the judicial/administrative area of the Immigration Office controlling/managing this.
GlossaryPage_ex_110: HR manager requested submission of Incheon Airport entry/exit confirmation documents for accurate visa history verification.
GlossaryPage_def_111: System under immigration law requiring foreigners staying 90+ days in Korea to register their personal info and address with the competent authority.
GlossaryPage_ex_111: Must complete foreign registration including fingerprinting within 90 days of entry to maintain legal long-term employment.
GlossaryPage_def_112: Official ID (Foreigner Registration Card) issued to long-term residents, equivalent to a Korean resident ID; carrying it is mandatory.
GlossaryPage_ex_112: Must receive a copy of the Foreign Registration Card for visual verification of personal details and legal visa status before payroll settlement.
GlossaryPage_def_113: International ID issued by the home government to prove nationality/identity, the most basic document for Korean entry/stay administration.
GlossaryPage_ex_113: Visual verification of the original, valid passport is always required during visa extensions or bank account opening.
GlossaryPage_def_114: Prior entry permit (visa stamp) granted by an embassy or MOJ confirming entry/stay possibility, marked with activity code (E-9, E-7, etc.).
GlossaryPage_ex_114: Providing labor and receiving money in Korea without a valid employment visa stamp is strictly prohibited by labor/immigration law.
GlossaryPage_def_115: Official business agreement between nations/agencies. In EPS, it refers to the MOU between the Korean MOEL and foreign labor-sending governments.
GlossaryPage_ex_115: Annual quotas are assigned based on EPS personnel introduction MOU conditions signed between the Korean government and the Vietnamese Ministry of Labor.
GlossaryPage_def_116: Sending nations (Vietnam, Philippines, Cambodia, etc., 16+ countries) that signed EPS agreements to officially select/send their labor to Korea.
GlossaryPage_ex_116: 3 new personnel selected/trained by the Cambodian government agency are scheduled to be assigned to our factory this year.
GlossaryPage_def_117: All administrative/educational preparation processes from local selection of a foreign worker to entry, training, and final placement.
GlossaryPage_ex_117: Foreigners entering under government EPS procedures must complete 3 days of mandatory취업 education before final site placement.
GlossaryPage_def_118: System where the income payer (company) withholds taxes from the worker's salary and pays them to the state (tax office) on the worker's behalf.
GlossaryPage_ex_118: Act of withholding income tax from the total payment and paying it on the worker's behalf every month.
GlossaryPage_def_119: Direct tax imposed by the state on net income from labor or business; calculated monthly based on salary income tax tables.
GlossaryPage_ex_119: Income tax (갑근세) item on the pay stub, with collection amount increasing proportionally to salary level and dependents.
GlossaryPage_def_120: Tax paid to the local government where the worker resides, separate from national income tax, pegged at 10% of the calculated income tax amount.
GlossaryPage_ex_120: If income tax withheld is 50,000 KRW, local income tax is automatically deducted as 5,000 KRW (10%).
GlossaryPage_def_121: Four social security insurances (Pension, Health, Employment, Industrial Accident) made mandatory by law for protection against social risks (old age, illness, etc.).
GlossaryPage_ex_121: All businesses with 1+ employees must register all eligible employees, including foreign workers, for the 4 major insurances.
GlossaryPage_def_122: State-operated income security system paying pensions for old age, disability, or death after paying premiums during economic activity.
GlossaryPage_ex_122: Under reciprocity, national pension enrollment is mandatory for nationals of agreement countries like Vietnam and Indonesia.
GlossaryPage_def_123: Mandatory social security system providing benefits for prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation of illness/injury.
GlossaryPage_ex_123: Foreign workers are registered as workplace subscribers upon entry; health insurance premiums are deducted from salary monthly.
GlossaryPage_def_124: Insurance supporting long-term care services for those struggling with daily life due to old age/illness; collected alongside health insurance premiums.
GlossaryPage_ex_124: Listed below health insurance on the pay stub, automatically calculated as [Health Premium Amount × Long-Term Care Rate].
GlossaryPage_def_125: Social insurance supporting stability during unemployment, job hunting support, and training cost coverage.
GlossaryPage_ex_125: E-9 foreign workers are not mandatorily enrolled but can apply for voluntary enrollment at the Employment Center.
GlossaryPage_def_126: Insurance covering treatment/livelihood costs for work-related injury/disease, with 100% premiums borne by the employer.
GlossaryPage_ex_126: A foreign worker injured by falling objects during loading can claim treatment costs and lost-wage compensation after insurance eligibility verification.
GlossaryPage_def_127: Deducting fixed/legal amounts (taxes, insurance, dorm fees, etc.) from total salary before payment.
GlossaryPage_ex_127: Summarized in the total deduction column of the monthly pay stub after withholding income tax and 4 major insurances.
GlossaryPage_def_128: State measures imposing taxes on specific wage items for fiscal revenue purposes.
GlossaryPage_ex_128: Most wage items directly received, such as base salary, overtime, and position allowances, are subject to taxation.
GlossaryPage_def_129: Income items excluded from the taxation/social insurance calculation base due to their nature as living support or reimbursement.
GlossaryPage_ex_129: Meal allowances under 200,000 KRW, vehicle maintenance under 200,000 KRW are representative legal tax-exempt items.
GlossaryPage_def_130: Specific money amount of tax calculated by multiplying the taxable standard by the rate, to be paid by the worker to the state.
GlossaryPage_ex_130: 35,400 KRW calculated as the final income tax for this month and deducted from payroll.
GlossaryPage_def_131: The ratio applied to the taxable amount; Korea adopts a progressive rate system where higher income is taxed at a higher rate.
GlossaryPage_ex_131: Income tax rates from 6% to 45% are applied differentially per income bracket and reflected in payroll deductions.
GlossaryPage_def_132: Duty of the tax payer or withholding agent (company) to formally submit tax calculation data to tax authorities.
GlossaryPage_ex_132: HR team must complete the withholding performance report to the tax office by the 10th of the month following salary payment.
GlossaryPage_def_133: Act of actually depositing the withheld tax amount (collected from salary) to the state/local treasury within the deadline.
GlossaryPage_ex_133: Aggregating the total income tax deducted from monthly salaries and paying it via the National Tax Service Hometax system by the 10th of the next month.
GlossaryPage_def_134: Adjustment process matching the temporarily paid amount (withholding) against the final actual amount confirmed by evidence.
GlossaryPage_ex_134: For mid-term retirees, the tax is recalculated based on the resignation month to refund or collect differences.
GlossaryPage_def_135: Annual mandatory state procedure matching the 1-year withholding total against the final confirmed tax after reflecting deductions/evidence.
GlossaryPage_ex_135: Foreign workers also submit year-end tax settlement documents around Jan-Feb, resulting in tax refunds or additional payments.
GlossaryPage_def_136: Act of returning excess taxes paid during the year when the final tax is confirmed to be less than the total withheld.
GlossaryPage_ex_136: Refund of 150,000 KRW received with the February salary after verification showed significant tax-deductible items.
GlossaryPage_def_137: Measure of collecting additional taxes when final tax confirmed is more than the total withheld during the year.
GlossaryPage_ex_137: 50,000 KRW deducted from salary due to additional tax obligation resulting from failing to submit all deduction evidence documents.
GlossaryPage_def_138: Mandatory foreign-only insurance for EPS where employers set aside a ratio of the monthly average wage to guarantee severance pay.
GlossaryPage_ex_138: Company regularly contributes to the 'Departure Maturity Insurance'; foreign workers claim/receive this instead of severance pay at the airport upon departure.
GlossaryPage_def_139: Mandatory foreign-only insurance the worker must enroll in upon entry to cover airfare costs for returning home.
GlossaryPage_ex_139: Worker must pay the one-time 'Return Cost Insurance' premium (approx. 400k-600k KRW) to the insurer within 3 months of entry.
GlossaryPage_def_140: Insurance mandatory by law for foreigners to be compensated for illness/injury occurring during weekends or daily life, outside of work.
GlossaryPage_ex_140: E-9 worker who broke a leg during a weekend soccer match can claim insurance benefits for surgery, as it's not a work-related accident.
GlossaryPage_def_141: Insurance mandatory for EPS employers to guarantee payment of unpaid wages in case of bankruptcy or financial difficulty.
GlossaryPage_ex_141: If wages are delayed due to company bankruptcy, the worker can claim the unpaid amount from the insurer after getting MOEL confirmation.
GlossaryPage_def_142: Statutory system paying 30 days' worth of average wage per year of service to employees working 15+ hours/week for 1+ year, upon resignation.
GlossaryPage_ex_142: Calculated days based on the last 3 months of salary to settle severance pay for a site member with 3 years of service.
GlossaryPage_def_143: Collective term for systems guaranteeing retirement income: legal severance, and retirement pension (DB, DC) funds accumulated monthly.
GlossaryPage_ex_143: Our factory operates a Defined Contribution (DC) plan, externally accumulating severance funds in worker-named accounts monthly.
GlossaryPage_def_144: Monetary goods paid under law to compensate for loss, treatment, and livelihood interruption due to work-related injury/death.
GlossaryPage_ex_144: Medical treatment benefit (covering hospital costs) paid directly by the Korea Workers' Compensation & Welfare Service after industrial accident approval.
GlossaryPage_def_145: Medical costs for treatment, such as consultation fees, surgery, hospitalization, and medication, to recover from work-related injuries.
GlossaryPage_ex_145: Processed claim for treatment costs under industrial accident benefits after collecting hospital receipts for eye surgery from a work-related accident.
GlossaryPage_def_146: Compensation paid by the state to support the livelihood of the worker/family during periods unable to work due to medical treatment.
GlossaryPage_ex_146: Applied to the KWCWS for temporary layoff benefits (70% of average wage) to compensate for wage loss during 20 days of hospitalization.
GlossaryPage_def_147: Compensation for permanent disability remaining after treatment ends, paid per disability grade (1-14).
GlossaryPage_ex_147: Received disability lump sum payment after KWCWS review, based on a disability diagnosis after losing a finger joint in a press accident.
GlossaryPage_def_148: Insurance for bereaved families if a worker dies from a work-related accident, paid to legal heirs.
GlossaryPage_ex_148: Proceeding with documentation notarization for the spouse living back home to verify survivor pension eligibility following a construction fall accident.
GlossaryPage_def_149: Act of permanently ending the employment relationship due to resignation, contract expiration, retirement, or dismissal.
GlossaryPage_ex_149: Confirmed resignation date for an E-9 worker whose stay permit expired, completing termination processes in the HR system.
GlossaryPage_def_150: Colloquial expression for ending employment, used interchangeably with 'resignation' in practical HR fields.
GlossaryPage_ex_150: Resignation confirmed for end of month after final approval of written resignation due to personal reasons and moving.
GlossaryPage_def_151: Legal act of dissolving the contract relationship for the future, such as dismissal or resignation during the contract.
GlossaryPage_ex_151: Employment contract can be terminated according to disciplinary procedures if a worker intentionally destroys company assets.
GlossaryPage_def_152: State where the employment contract relationship officially ends for legal reasons.
GlossaryPage_ex_152: Started severance settlement and documentation as the contract period for project workers concluded.
GlossaryPage_def_153: Automatic expiration of employment validity when the contract deadline passes.
GlossaryPage_ex_153: Contract period for a 1-year contract worker has expired; HR committee is discussing renewal.
GlossaryPage_def_154: Quitting before the contract deadline due to resignation or mutual agreement.
GlossaryPage_ex_154: Example of a worker quitting after 6 months on a 3-year E-9 contract to return home due to a parent's illness.
GlossaryPage_def_155: Worker expressing intent to end employment, typically via written resignation to acquire legal validity.
GlossaryPage_ex_155: Conveyed resignation intent to the department head and submitted written resignation to the HR team due to personal health/job change.
GlossaryPage_def_156: Statutory duty under Article 26 of Labor Standards Act to notify dismissal at least 30 days in advance.
GlossaryPage_ex_156: Failure to provide 30-day notice requires immediate payment of 30 days' normal wage to avoid legal punishment.
GlossaryPage_def_157: Wages that must be paid immediately if the 30-day notice obligation is not met during dismissal.
GlossaryPage_ex_157: Settled 'Dismissal Notice Allowance' equivalent to 1 month's normal wage for a worker dismissed immediately due to management difficulties.
GlossaryPage_def_158: Timing of full return home after employment ends, at which point the Departure Maturity Insurance is claimed.
GlossaryPage_ex_158: Prepared refund claim documents for maturity insurance, aligned with the end of the 4-year 10-month E-9 visa term.
GlossaryPage_def_159: Wage debt remaining unpaid due to company circumstances or errors, despite labor being provided.
GlossaryPage_ex_159: Retroactively reflected 150,000 KRW in unpaid wages found due to night shift calculation errors in last month's salary.
GlossaryPage_def_160: Illegal status of unpaid wages accumulated beyond the legal deadline, with the employer failing to pay in full.
GlossaryPage_ex_160: A labor dispute arose when the Labor Office received a petition due to two months of unpaid wages for all employees.
GlossaryPage_def_161: Procedure of calculating final salary, tax, and insurance differences when a worker resigns mid-period.
GlossaryPage_ex_161: Calculated daily salary and used settlement program to confirm net payment for a worker resigning on the 15th.
GlossaryPage_def_162: HR practice of systematically recording/controlling attendance, leave, overtime, etc., as baseline data for payroll and evaluation.
GlossaryPage_ex_162: Since PayLens was introduced, attendance management for foreign workers has been automated based on mobile fingerprint records.
GlossaryPage_def_163: Digital proof data of arrival/departure times recorded in systems.
GlossaryPage_ex_163: Operators must leave attendance records at the gate reader for accurate overtime settlement.
GlossaryPage_def_164: Specific work orders and manufacturing specifications assigned to workers by managers to meet daily targets.
GlossaryPage_ex_164: At morning roll call, the foreman displayed the work instruction sheet translated into Vietnamese on the monitor to announce daily targets.
GlossaryPage_def_165: Assigning personnel to specific processes (assembly, inspection, packaging) considering skills/physical condition.
GlossaryPage_ex_165: Placed a meticulous new hire in inspection and a strong worker in logistics loading.
GlossaryPage_def_166: System of mandatory periodic safety education on machinery, rules, and evacuation under the Industrial Safety and Health Act.
GlossaryPage_ex_166: Provided image-based safety education videos in foreign languages to new foreign hires to prevent language-barrier accidents.
GlossaryPage_def_167: Protective gear (helmet, safety shoes, goggles, masks, earplugs) to protect the body from risks.
GlossaryPage_ex_167: Must wear earplugs in the press factory to prevent hearing loss.
GlossaryPage_def_168: Activities to remove risk factors, protect life/health, and create a comfortable work environment.
GlossaryPage_ex_168: Maintaining the highest safety rating through regular inspection and preventive measures.
GlossaryPage_def_169: Procedure of documenting the cause, damage, and measures taken immediately after an accident.
GlossaryPage_ex_169: Reported to the factory manager via accident report attached with witness statements and site photos after a forklift collision.
GlossaryPage_def_170: Guide text on danger factors/rules that workers must remember to reduce defects or prevent accidents.
GlossaryPage_ex_170: Attached 3-language safety stickers on chemical injectors so foreign workers can easily understand.
GlossaryPage_def_171: Process of measuring/testing to confirm if a product meets company quality standards.
GlossaryPage_ex_171: Passed final quality inspection using calipers to measure dimensional error before packaging.
GlossaryPage_def_172: Defective product status not saleable or usable due to errors/damage.
GlossaryPage_ex_172: Half of the plastic cases produced this morning were discarded due to molding temperature failure.
GlossaryPage_def_173: Act of customer returning products due to discovered defects/mismatch.
GlossaryPage_ex_173: Called emergency meeting after 5,000 units were returned by an auto vendor due to dimensional errors.
GlossaryPage_def_174: Act of modifying/re-processing defective products if they can be turned into valid items.
GlossaryPage_ex_174: Organized a rework team to sand and re-spray panels with paint aggregation issues.
GlossaryPage_def_175: Quantitative results of labor input, such as completion quantity or goal achievement rate.
GlossaryPage_ex_175: Foremen consolidate data on net production and defect rates to update the daily performance board.
GlossaryPage_def_176: Specific quantity/weight of products produced by a factory line/equipment.
GlossaryPage_ex_176: Total production increased by 20% compared to last month due to stable raw material supply.
GlossaryPage_def_177: Target quantity planned to be produced within specific working hours (e.g., 8 hours).
GlossaryPage_ex_177: Today's day-shift target is 2,000 units, so line speed must be maintained to avoid overtime.
GlossaryPage_def_178: Document (under Art 48) providing calculation methods and deductions, mandatory for employer to hand to worker upon payment.
GlossaryPage_ex_178: PayLens automatically sends multilingual digital pay stubs to foreign workers' smartphones.
GlossaryPage_def_179: Mandatory HR ledger storing personal info (name, DOB, history, entry date) kept at the business site.
GlossaryPage_ex_179: Updated the worker ledger with visa expiration dates to prepare for labor inspections.
GlossaryPage_def_180: Attendance ledger (manual/digital) proving daily attendance/departure times.
GlossaryPage_ex_180: Backing up gate computer attendance data as source evidence for monthly payroll settlement.
GlossaryPage_def_181: Core corporate accounting ledger recording salary payments and tax deductions, mandatory to preserve for 3 years.
GlossaryPage_ex_181: Proceeding with wage ledger approval for accounting audit and payroll transfer authorization.
GlossaryPage_def_182: Form submitted for management approval before overtime/holiday work, including reasons/estimated time.
GlossaryPage_ex_182: Workers must submit electronic overtime requests by 4 PM to get overtime recognized.
GlossaryPage_def_183: Common HR document for applying for annual/sick/consolation leave, for approval by supervisor.
GlossaryPage_ex_183: Submitted leave request for hometown visit confirmed 2 weeks in advance to allow for replacement scheduling.
GlossaryPage_def_184: Standard form for expressing intent to resign and official last working day.
GlossaryPage_ex_184: Submitted resignation letter signed by the worker to HR one month in advance, considering handover time.
GlossaryPage_def_185: Document communicating disciplinary decisions (pay cut, warning, suspension, dismissal) and reasons.
GlossaryPage_ex_185: Sent disciplinary notice via registered mail/digital systems for severe violation of service rules due to 5 days of unauthorized absence.
GlossaryPage_ex_186: Collected signed move-in confirmations after instructing dorm residents on facility damage rules.
GlossaryPage_def_187: Document proving worker's legal consent for administrative processing, data usage, or work rules.
GlossaryPage_ex_187: Collected pre-consent for overtime/holiday work from all employees upon entry to prevent legal disputes.
GlossaryPage_def_188: Administrative document submitted to agencies (labor, tax, immigration) reporting changes.
GlossaryPage_ex_188: Submitted employment change report to the Employment Center via fax as the worker moved to a different factory.
GlossaryPage_def_189: Official document issued by company/agency proving employment, career, or qualification.
GlossaryPage_ex_189: Worker requested proof of employment and withholding tax statement from HR for an apartment loan extension.
GlossaryPage_def_190: Information flyer for employees explaining rule/benefit changes or administrative deadlines.
GlossaryPage_ex_190: Posted translated notices on factory boards about changes to cafeteria operation times and meal ticket processes.
GlossaryPage_def_191: Document form (groupware/intranet) communicating major company news or management guidelines.
GlossaryPage_ex_191: Posted notice on the groupware main screen regarding factory shutdown and security check rules for Chuseok.
GlossaryPage_def_192: Document for vowing compliance with security/secrecy/safety rules and accepting liability for violations.
GlossaryPage_ex_192: Collected nondisclosure agreements from R&D and core line staff to prevent recipe/blueprint leakage.
GlossaryPage_def_193: Illegal act of not paying wages/severance within the legal deadline (payment date or 14 days after resignation).
GlossaryPage_ex_193: Delaying salary payment intentionally violates the Labor Standards Act; workers can petition the Labor Office for relief.

PreAnalysisPage_description: For an accurate wage theft review, answer the four questions below. The legal standards that apply will change based on your answers.
PreAnalysisPage_q1_title: Is the company’s regular workforce 5 or more?
PreAnalysisPage_q1_info: Legal basis: choosing "Yes" enables overtime, night, and holiday pay premium calculations (1.5x).
PreAnalysisPage_q2_title: Is the agreed weekly working time 15 hours or more?
PreAnalysisPage_q2_info: Legal basis: choosing "Yes" confirms eligibility for weekly holiday pay and includes it in the calculation.
PreAnalysisPage_q3_title: Has the continuous employment period been 1 year or more?
PreAnalysisPage_q3_info: Legal basis: choosing "Yes" enables severance pay calculations.
PreAnalysisPage_q4_title: Have there been days you unexpectedly had to take off because of company circumstances?
PreAnalysisPage_q4_info: Legal basis: choosing "Yes" reviews the possibility of claiming shutdown allowance (70% of average wages).
